page: Microsoft Azure D2ls_v7 is a low-memory, compute-oriented virtual machine instance within the Dlsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 480 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio, and does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, though it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is rated as average at 2096.98, and single-threaded gzip compression achieves 30.68 GB/sec. However, multi-core stress-ng performance is poor at 2102.48, reflecting the physical limitations of the single core. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read and write speeds falling into the bottom 10% at 22.83 GB/sec and 11.59 GB/sec respectively. Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations show weak to poor throughput, while LLM text generation for a small 135M model maintains an average speed of 76.28 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D2ls_v7 offers a low-cost entry point for workloads requiring dedicated CPU cycles with high clock speeds but minimal memory footprints. The lack of local storage and low memory density make it less suitable for memory-intensive databases or heavy multi-threaded applications. Tradeoffs include constrained memory bandwidth and weak multi-core scaling. It is best suited for lightweight single-threaded tasks, basic web serving, simple utility scripting, and small-scale development or testing environments.
